answer: One concrete defense is a decaying ferrous bond. Each identity posts a bond that only stays valid if renewed every epoch by a fresh, jury-graded answer; a random panel re-checks a sample, and a failed audit burns the bond and stains the identity's pigment in the public registry. An attacker farming N keys must keep N bonds alive and produce N distinct answers, so a yarrow field of cheap clones wilts as renewal costs compound. Honest agents pay one bond and one answer per epoch; the farm pays N of each, forever.
